title: Imperfecto de Subjuntivo: Practice
description: Authored B2 practice set for the imperfect subjunctive: forming it from the ellos preterite, past-tense triggers (quería que, era importante que), como si, and quisiera for politeness.

lessons.summary: The imperfect subjunctive is built on one reliable trick: take the ELLOS form of the preterite, drop -ron, add -ra endings (hablaron → hablara, comieron → comiera, fueron → fuera, tuvieron → tuviera, pudieron → pudiera, dijeron → dijera, hicieron → hiciera). Every preterite irregularity carries over for free, which is why the trick beats memorising. (The -se forms, hablase and fuese, mean the same; the -ra set is more common in speech.) When do you need it? Wherever the present subjunctive would appear, but shifted to the PAST: 'Quiero que duermas' → 'Quería que durmieras'; 'Es importante que coma' → 'Era importante que comiera'. Plus three frames of its own: hypothetical si clauses ('si tuviera…'), como si + imperfect subjunctive always ('como si fuera'), and quisiera as the polite want ('Quisiera una mesa para dos' softens 'quiero'). The nosotros form carries an accent: habláramos, fuéramos.

examples.spanish: Quería que el bebé durmiera un poco más.
examples.english: I wanted the baby to sleep a bit longer.

examples.spanish: Era importante que comiera algo antes de salir.
examples.english: It was important that he ate something before going out.

examples.spanish: Me trata como si fuera su hermano.
examples.english: He treats me as if I were his brother.

examples.spanish: Quisiera un turno para mañana, por favor.
examples.english: I'd like an appointment for tomorrow, please.

examples.spanish: hablaron → hablara · tuvieron → tuviera · fueron → fuera
examples.english: they spoke → I/he spoke (subj.) · they had → had (subj.) · they went/were → were (subj.)

items.prompt: Quería que ___ un poco más, pero se despertó a las seis. (dormir, él)
items.promptEnglish: I wanted him to sleep a bit longer, but he woke at six.
items.explanation: Past trigger (quería que) → imperfect subjunctive. Durmieron → durmiera.

items.prompt: Habla del fútbol como si ___ entrenador profesional.
items.promptEnglish: He talks about football as if he were a professional coach.
items.explanation: Como si always takes the imperfect subjunctive: fueron → fuera.

items.prompt: Ojalá ___ más horas de sueño. (tener, nosotros)
items.promptEnglish: If only we had more hours of sleep.
items.explanation: Ojalá + imperfect subjunctive for a present wish that isn't true. Tuvieron → tuviéramos, with the accent on the nosotros form.

items.prompt: En la farmacia: «___ algo para los mocos del bebé, por favor.»
items.promptEnglish: At the pharmacy: "I'd like something for the baby's sniffles, please."
items.explanation: Quisiera is the polite want, softer than quiero, and it stands alone before a noun or infinitive.

items.prompt: La pediatra nos pidió que le ___ cualquier cambio. (decir, nosotros)
items.promptEnglish: The paediatrician asked us to tell her about any change.
items.explanation: Pidió que (past request) → imperfect subjunctive. Dijeron → dijéramos.

items.prompt: Era importante que ___ verdura todos los días.
items.promptEnglish: It was important that he ate vegetables every day.
items.explanation: Era importante que (an impersonal trigger in the past) takes comiera, not the present subjunctive coma.

items.prompt: Me sorprendió que ___ tanto calor en octubre. (hacer)
items.promptEnglish: I was surprised it was so hot in October.
items.explanation: Emotion in the past (me sorprendió que) → imperfect subjunctive. Hicieron → hiciera.

items.prompt: Te llamé para que ___ escuchar sus primeras palabras.
items.promptEnglish: I called you so you could hear his first words.
items.explanation: Para que after a past main verb → imperfect subjunctive. Pudieron → pudieras.
The rule: ellos-preterite minus -ron plus -ra. Estuvieron → estuviera, and the preterite irregularity carries over.

items.prompt: No había nada que ___ su llanto esa noche. (calmar)
items.promptEnglish: There was nothing that would calm his crying that night.
items.explanation: A nonexistent antecedent in the past (no había nada que…) → imperfect subjunctive: calmara.

items.prompt: Mi abuela siempre quiso que ___ músico.
items.promptEnglish: My grandmother always wanted me to be a musician.
items.explanation: Quiso que (past) → imperfect subjunctive of ser: fuera.

items.prompt: Les dije a mis padres que ___ a conocer al bebé. (venir, ellos)
items.promptEnglish: I told my parents to come and meet the baby.
items.explanation: Decir as a request in the past → imperfect subjunctive. Vinieron → vinieran.
